notes:
=== LaZagne - Comprehensive Application Credential Extraction ===
Sweeps dozens of application credential stores in a single pass - highest breadth of any single tool.

=== COVERAGE ===
Web browsers: Chrome, Firefox, IE/Edge, Opera, Brave → saved passwords
Chat clients: Skype, Teams, Discord → saved session tokens
Databases: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQLite → saved connection credentials
Email clients: Outlook, Thunderbird → account passwords
VPN configs: Cisco, OpenVPN, Juniper → VPN authentication material
WiFi passwords: Windows wireless profiles → PSKs
Windows credential stores: Autologon, Credential Manager, DPAPI blobs, LSA secrets
Developer tools: git credentials, SVN auth files, Maven settings.xml
Remote access: WinSCP, FileZilla (overlaps with SessionGopher)
Sysadmin tools: MobaXterm, Royal TS connection manager

=== USAGE ===
All modules:
  .\lazagne.exe all
  .\lazagne.exe all -vv   (verbose - shows why items were skipped)

Specific category (reduces noise, useful for stealth):
  .\lazagne.exe browsers
  .\lazagne.exe databases
  .\lazagne.exe windows

Save output to file:
  .\lazagne.exe all -oJ -output C:\Temp\   (JSON format)

=== OPERATIONAL NOTES ===
Runs in the context of the current user - only extracts credentials accessible to that user
After privilege escalation: run again as SYSTEM or admin to access service account credential stores
AV frequently flags LaZagne - consider compiling from source with modified strings
Event ID 4688 (process creation) generated when LaZagne runs if audit is enabled

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
LaZagne → database credentials → SQL server access → lateral movement
LaZagne → VPN credentials → access to VPN-protected segments
LaZagne → git credentials → code repositories → source code, API keys, secrets
LaZagne → Teams/Slack tokens → session hijacking → internal communication access
After each new account compromise → run LaZagne again (credential stores are user-specific)

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Running as a service account (e.g., after web shell) → may have stored DB credentials
IT admin accounts → highest yield (admin tools, VPN configs, multiple server passwords)
Developer accounts → git credentials, IDE stored passwords, cloud CLI configs (AWS, Azure)

recommended.note: Manual complement to the automated sweep.
Targeted grab of saved session/RDP/PuTTY creds.

name: Credential Hunting - LaZagne (All Modules)
description: LaZagne recovers stored passwords from browsers, mail clients, Wi-Fi, RDP, databases, and many apps in one run.

defense.why_it_works: LaZagne queries dozens of Windows credential stores: browser saved passwords (Chrome, Firefox, IE), database clients (MySQL, PostgreSQL), sysadmin tools (PuTTY, WinSCP, FileZilla), email clients, Wi-Fi passwords, and Windows Credential Manager. All modules run in one command with `all`, dumping every recoverable credential in a single sweep.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as the target user (credentials recovered are that user's). Admin rights for some modules (system-level credential stores). LaZagne binary present on system.
defense.impact: Mass credential recovery from all applications used by the compromised user. May recover passwords for VPN, RDP, SSH, web services, databases - enabling extensive lateral movement.
defense.detection: LaZagne.exe execution (known bad binary - 47/70 AV detection on VirusTotal). Unusual reads to browser credential stores (Login Data, logins.json). Credential store access from non-browser process. EDR: credential dumping behavior pattern.
defense.artifacts: Process log: lazagne.exe executed | EDR: credential store access by non-browser process | AV alert: LaZagne signature | Network: if credentials used shortly after recovery
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (Image="*lazagne*" OR OriginalFileName="*LaZagne*" OR CommandLine="*lazagne*all*")
| table _time, Computer, User, CommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has "lazagne" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName has "LaZagne" or ProcessCommandLine has "lazagne"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention: Deploy endpoint detection capable of identifying credential harvesting tool patterns. Restrict write/execute access to C:\Windows\Temp and other staging directories. Use browser-based MFA to prevent saved password reuse. Manage secrets in enterprise password managers with access controls.
defense.misconfiguration: No endpoint protection blocking known credential dumping tools. Users storing credentials in browsers without MFA. No monitoring on credential store access by non-browser processes.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# LaZagne runs all modules:
.\lazagne.exe all
# Output: Chrome passwords, PuTTY sessions, FileZilla creds, etc.
defense.secure_config:
# Deploy EDR with credential access detection
# Block known LaZagne hashes via AV/WDAC
# Enforce MFA on all services so stolen passwords require second factor

# Browser credential hardening:
# Chrome: enable Safe Browsing Enhanced Protection
# Enforce Enterprise Password Manager policies

# Monitor: reads to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data by non-Chrome processes
defense.evasion: Copy the credential store (browser Login Data, .kdbx, PSReadline history) and decrypt/crack it OFFLINE rather than running signatured binaries (LaZagne/SharpChrome) on the host; scope searches to likely paths to limit disk I/O; use built-in cmdlets over dropped tools.

validation.success_criteria: Expected log events appear in the configured SIEM within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Only browsers
variations.description: Runs LaZagne to extract stored passwords from web browsers. Recovers saved credentials from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and other browsers on the target.

variations.label: Write to file
variations.description: Runs LaZagne to extract stored credentials from all supported applications. Harvests passwords from browsers, email clients, databases, sysadmin tools, and WiFi profiles on the compromised host.

explain:
Recovers locally stored application passwords in one run:
  .\lazagne.exe all        run every module (browsers, mail clients, Wi-Fi, RDP, databases, and more)
Each module reads its app's own credential store in the current user's context; use browsers to scope it, or -oN -output to write results to a file.
